scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: You take a call on a busy road, and the other person hears you clearly. Where did all that traffic noise go?

scenes.name: mics
scenes.text: Your phone has more than one microphone. Usually one near your mouth, and others at the top or back.

scenes.name: compare
scenes.text: Your voice is much louder in the bottom mic. Traffic noise reaches all the mics at about the same level.

scenes.name: focus
scenes.text: By comparing them, the phone works out which sounds come from your mouth, and focuses on that direction.

scenes.name: suppress
scenes.text: Noise suppression software, often trained on thousands of hours of audio, then cuts the steady background noise out.

scenes.name: echo
scenes.text: It also removes the other person's voice coming out of your speaker, so they don't hear an echo of themselves.

scenes.name: send
scenes.text: The cleaned voice is compressed and sent over the network. All of this happens live, while you talk.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Mics, compare, focus, clean. Just your voice. Follow for more on how things really work.
